title: Grade 11 Chemistry — Redox Reactions & Electrochemistry Basics
description: Oxidation states, oxidation-reduction, balancing redox equations, electrochemical cells
subject: chemistry

questions.question: Oxidation is defined as:
options: Gain of electrons (or gain of oxygen, or loss of hydrogen)
Loss of electrons (or loss of hydrogen, or gain of oxygen)
questions.explanation: Oxidation = loss of electrons (LEO: Loss of Electrons = Oxidation). OR: gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, increase in oxidation state. GER = Gain of Electrons = Reduction.

questions.question: In the reaction: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, which species is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Zn: 0 → +2 (loses 2e⁻) = oxidised. Cu²⁺: +2 → 0 (gains 2e⁻) = reduced. Zn is the reducing agent (causes Cu²⁺ to be reduced). Cu²⁺ is the oxidising agent (causes Zn to be oxidised).

questions.question: The oxidation state of sulphur in H₂SO₄ is:
The oxidation state of Mn in KMnO₄ is:
questions.explanation: KMnO₄: K = +1, O = −2 (×4 = −8). Sum = 0: 1 + Mn − 8 = 0 → Mn = +7. KMnO₄ is a strong oxidising agent (purple colour).

questions.question: In an electrochemical (galvanic) cell, oxidation occurs at the:
questions.explanation: Galvanic cell: ANODE = oxidation (negative electrode); CATHODE = reduction (positive electrode). Mnemonic: ANOX (Anode = Oxidation); REDCAT (Reduction = Cathode).

questions.question: The standard electrode potential (E°) of the standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) is:
questions.explanation: The Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE): H₂(g) → 2H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻, E° = 0.00 V (defined). All other electrode potentials are measured relative to SHE.

questions.question: A disproportionation reaction is one in which the same element is simultaneously:
questions.explanation: Disproportionation: same element is BOTH oxidised AND reduced. Example: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O. Cl goes from 0 → −1 (reduced, in NaCl) AND 0 → +1 (oxidised, in NaOCl).

questions.question: The EMF of a galvanic cell is: E_cell = ?
questions.explanation: E_cell = E_cathode (reduction) − E_anode (reduction). A positive E_cell indicates a spontaneous reaction. For Zn-Cu cell: E_cell = +0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.

questions.question: The role of the salt bridge in a galvanic cell is to:
options: Complete the electrical circuit by allowing ion flow, maintaining electrical neutrality in both half-cells
questions.explanation: Salt bridge (KCl, KNO₃ in agar): allows ions to flow between half-cells to maintain electrical neutrality. Without it, the cell would stop working (one half-cell becomes negatively charged, the other positive).

questions.question: The oxidation state of N in NH₃ is:
questions.explanation: NH₃: H = +1 (×3 = +3). Sum = 0: N + 3 = 0 → N = −3. In HNO₃: N is +5. In NO: N is +2. Nitrogen has multiple oxidation states (−3 to +5).

questions.question: In electrolysis, which reaction occurs at the cathode?
options: Reduction (cations gain electrons and are deposited/reduced)
questions.explanation: Electrolysis cathode = reduction (cations migrate to cathode and gain electrons). Anode = oxidation (anions lose electrons). In CuSO₄ electrolysis: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu at cathode; Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ at anode.

questions.question: Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis states that the mass deposited (m) is:
options: Proportional to charge passed (m ∝ Q = It)
questions.explanation: Faraday's 1st Law: m = (M/nF) × Q = (M × I × t)/(nF). Where M = molar mass, n = electrons transferred, F = 96,485 C/mol (Faraday's constant), I = current, t = time.

questions.question: Oxidising agents are substances that:
options: Get reduced (gain electrons) and thereby oxidise the other substance
questions.explanation: Oxidising agents accept electrons (are themselves reduced). Examples: O₂, KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇, F₂, H₂O₂. Reducing agents donate electrons (are oxidised). Examples: H₂, C, Na, reducing metals.

questions.question: The change in oxidation state of Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇ when it acts as an oxidising agent is:
questions.explanation: In K₂Cr₂O₇: Cr = +6 (strong oxidising agent). When reduced: Cr³⁺ (green). Change: +6 → +3. Each Cr gains 3e⁻. Two Cr per formula unit: total 6e⁻ gained.

questions.question: Corrosion of iron (rusting) is an electrochemical process because:
options: Iron acts as anode (oxidised to Fe²⁺) and oxygen acts at cathode (reduced), with water as electrolyte
Rusting only occurs at high temperatures
questions.explanation: Rusting is an electrochemical process: Fe(anode) → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻ (oxidation); O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻ (cathode, reduction). Fe²⁺ + OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₂ → Fe₂O₃·nH₂O (rust). Water + O₂ are needed.
